summary: Italy, China, France and Spain come fast, Germany, India, Mexico and the UK with a little thought, and Russia and Iran are the stretch. Greece, Egypt, Japan and the US are where the lives go.
reasons: A casual found 8 in 13 guesses (a second ordering found 6), losing lives on Greece (#16, 21), Egypt (#53, 7), Japan and the US (both #11, 27) and Peru, each with its count; Egypt's 7 is the surprise. A fan found all 10 with 4 lives lost.

The totals read right: every row of the five regional tables adds up (cultural + natural + mixed), no state is on two pages, and a shared site counts for each country, as the prompt says. No tie at #10/#11 (Iran 30, Japan and the US 27).
Shares 6 of its 10 answers with Most visited countries (France, Spain, Italy, Mexico, the UK, Germany): run them weeks apart. Blitz: all 32 casual names scored.
fixes: Russia's fact is wrong, fix before it runs: Russia's first sites in 1990 were three (Kremlin and Red Square, Historic Centre of Saint Petersburg, Kizhi Pogost); the five were the whole Soviet Union's, with Kyiv's Saint Sophia and Khiva's Itchan Kala. In scripts/facts/world-heritage-countries.json, for example: "Its first three sites, the Kremlin and Red Square among them, were listed in 1990, while it was still part of the Soviet Union."
